title: Amount Input
summary: A money field that groups digits as you type, spells the amount out and flags an amount about ten times off the usual one.
description: Groups digits live with Intl.NumberFormat (lakh/crore for en-IN), spells the amount cheque-style, and when you pass `typical` warns about an amount `threshold`× (default 10×) above or below it, with a one-tap fix for a zero slip. Reports a number plus the exact decimal and minor-unit strings.
catches: An extra or missing zero, when the amount is `threshold`× (default 10) or more off the `typical` value you pass, with a one-tap fix that moves the zeros exactly
A paste in another locale's format ("1.250,50", "1.250.000", "12,5" in an en-IN field), by asking which reading you meant
Hard-to-read long numbers, by grouping digits as you type (Indian grouping for en-IN)
Misread amounts, by spelling the amount out in words
Leading zeros, and digits beyond `maxDigits` or the currency's precision, with a visible hint when digits are dropped
limits: The warning needs a `typical` amount; there is no fallback to a balance, limit or last amount
The number passed to onValueChange is a JavaScript float; use the second argument's `decimal` or `minor` string (or the hidden input's decimal string) for exact money maths
The paste check runs only when the paste replaces the whole field, and only for '.' and ',' separators
Default words are English ("Rupees … only", "paise", English unit names); pass `wordsFormatter` for other languages
Defaults to en-IN and INR; set locale and currency for other markets
a11y: aria-describedby lists only the words and notice elements that are currently rendered, plus any id you pass
Warnings, the truncation hint and the paste question are in an aria-live="polite" region; the fix and paste buttons return focus to the input
The animated read-back respects prefers-reduced-motion (motion's useReducedMotion)
server: Validate amount and currency on the server, derive payable amounts from trusted data and use idempotency keys; this warning is a review prompt, not a correctness check.
